reply.recognition: Recognized from the supplied documentation as the public UCI Student Performance dataset (UCI 320), with Portuguese-language records and the cited Cortez and Silva 2008 introduction. This recognition comes from the input; no external source or remembered result is being used as evidence.
reply.summary: Goal: choose support at the end of period 1 for students whose G1 result indicates academic risk, and evaluate learning by the period-2 grade G2 (0-20 points) and attendance during the intervening period. The input describes 649 student records from two Portuguese schools, including G1/G2, absences, travel-time category, study-time category, and existing school/family/paid support indicators. It documents temporal grades and notes that support was not randomized; survey timing is limited. New increment proposed here: distinguish an access-to-instruction bottleneck from a subject-mastery bottleneck by comparing equal-contact attendance-recovery support with tutoring in a prospective randomized school pilot. The dataset can motivate and help scope the question, but cannot identify causal effects or verify the proposed mechanism.

candidates.title: Separate attendance-access support from tutoring at the first-period decision point
candidates.question: Among students below the school's predeclared Portuguese pass threshold at G1, does an equal-contact attendance-access and missed-lesson recovery package improve G2 more than subject tutoring, especially for students with high period-1 absence counts or long travel times?
candidates.new_claim: A useful support decision may depend on whether missed instructional time or difficulty mastering attended lessons is the more important bottleneck. This is a testable mechanism hypothesis, not a finding in the supplied data.
candidates.input_delta: The input provides period grades, absence counts, a coarse travel-time category, and existing support indicators, but does not compare support types under random assignment or measure dated attendance and instructional exposure. The proposal adds a direct equal-contact comparison and an attendance mediator.
candidates.domain_value: A school could direct limited added support toward access and catch-up when absence is the binding constraint, and use tutoring when attendance is adequate but mastery remains low.
known_basis_refs: official_documentation.additional_info: G1/G2 are first/second-period grades and G3 is final grade; G1/G2 correlate with G3
official_documentation.variables: absences, traveltime, schoolsup, G1, G2
case.workflow: support allocation beyond final-grade prediction
case.unit: two Portuguese schools; no randomized support assignment; limited survey timing metadata
assumptions: The school's existing pass threshold can be specified before enrollment and is meaningful for this course.
Schools can deliver two added-support options with the same scheduled contact time without replacing legally or ethically required support.
Attendance-access support can be operationalized consistently, and individual attendance and intervention exposure can be recorded during the period.
Randomization can be conducted within school and baseline-risk strata, with analysis accounting for classroom or teacher clustering.
candidates.variables_and_units: Eligibility: G1 below a school-predeclared Portuguese pass threshold (grade points, 0-20). Baseline risk: scheduled class periods missed during period 1 (count) and travel time in minutes, newly measured rather than relying only on the input's 1-4 bins. Randomized added-support offer: access-and-catch-up package versus subject tutoring, with equal scheduled contact minutes per student. Intermediate outcome: attended scheduled Portuguese lessons during period 2 (count and proportion). Primary outcome: G2 Portuguese grade points (0-20). Unit: student, with school/classroom clustering in assignment or inference.
candidates.testable_prediction: Frozen before any tool return: relative to equal-contact tutoring, the access-and-catch-up offer will produce a larger period-2 attendance increase and a larger mean G2 gain among eligible students in the predeclared high-absence stratum than among eligible students with low absence. If it improves attendance but not G2, the claim that access recovery is a more useful learning support is not supported.
candidates.alternative: The main bottleneck is subject mastery rather than missed instruction, or both packages work only through attention and contact time; tutoring will match or exceed the access package on G2, and attendance changes will not explain any difference.
candidates.discriminating_test: Run a preregistered, equal-contact randomized comparison among eligible students at the end of period 1, stratified by school and predeclared absence-risk stratum. Record dated scheduled and attended lessons, package delivery, G1, and G2. Estimate intention-to-treat differences in attendance and G2 and the treatment-by-baseline-absence interaction, with uncertainty intervals and classroom-aware inference. Set a school-relevant minimum G2 difference and analysis rule before enrollment. An attendance advantage without a G2 advantage favors the alternative that access alone is insufficient; a G2 advantage concentrated among high-absence students and accompanied by attendance improvement supports the proposed routing hypothesis, but mediation itself needs additional assumptions.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Only exploratory feasibility checks: determine whether G1/G2, absences, and traveltime have usable variation and whether a proposed high-absence subgroup is large enough to motivate prospective recruitment. Existing observational support comparisons cannot estimate the randomized contrast.
candidates.required_new_data: Prospective student-level eligibility and baseline G1; dated period-1 and period-2 scheduled/attended lesson counts; actual commute minutes or a validated travel-barrier measure; randomized offer and assignment stratum; delivered contact minutes and package fidelity; G2; school/class identifiers; and a predeclared pass threshold, minimum relevant grade difference, and analysis plan.
candidates.failure_condition: The proposal is not supported if, in a sufficiently precise randomized comparison, access-and-catch-up does not improve G2 relative to equal-contact tutoring in the high-absence stratum, or if the predicted attendance increase is absent. If attendance rises without a meaningful G2 difference, reject the stronger claim that attendance recovery alone is the more effective academic support.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Search for secondary-school randomized or quasi-randomized comparisons of attendance or transport-barrier interventions with missed-instruction recovery versus equal-dose subject tutoring, testing baseline-absence moderation and attendance as a mediator of period-grade outcomes.

candidates.title: Test whether a brief student-led needs check improves support matching
candidates.question: At the end of period 1, does a brief structured student conversation that identifies the main barrier and routes the student to the matching existing support improve period-2 support uptake and G2 compared with usual referral among students below the school's predeclared threshold?
candidates.new_claim: The value of a support offer may depend on matching it to a student's stated barrier; collecting a brief barrier assessment could improve the match even without increasing total support minutes.
candidates.input_delta: The input contains broad support indicators and household or school-context variables, but no student-stated need, referral pathway, support-match quality, uptake timing, or randomized test of routing.
candidates.domain_value: Schools could improve the use of existing tutoring, attendance, or family-contact resources by reducing referrals to supports that students do not need or cannot use.
known_basis_refs: official_documentation.variables: schoolsup, famsup, paid, absences, G1, G2
case.workflow: useful support understanding or allocation
case.unit: no randomized support assignment; limited survey timing metadata
assumptions: Students can report a useful primary barrier in a short, non-stigmatizing conversation.
The school has at least two actionable support routes and can record offers and uptake.
A usual-referral comparison is ethically acceptable and does not withhold standard support.
candidates.variables_and_units: At-risk eligibility by predeclared G1 threshold (0-20 grade points); student-reported primary barrier (categorical, collected at period-1 end); routing offer and uptake (categorical and yes/no, with dates); support contact time (minutes); G2 (0-20 grade points). Unit: student, clustered by school or class.
candidates.testable_prediction: Compared with usual referral, the needs-check group will have a higher proportion accepting and attending the support route matched to the reported barrier, with a larger G2 gain if matching improves effective support exposure.
candidates.alternative: The conversation adds attention but does not improve actual match or uptake; any G2 difference is explained by contact time or novelty rather than barrier-specific routing.
candidates.discriminating_test: Randomize eligible students to structured needs-check and routing or usual referral, keep available support minutes the same, preregister matched-route uptake as the proximal outcome and G2 as the academic outcome, and compare intention-to-treat effects. Collect reasons for non-uptake and test whether the proposed route was actually delivered.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: No causal or matching test is feasible. The input may describe existing support prevalence, but not needs, offers, uptake, or temporal support routing.
candidates.required_new_data: Student-reported barrier at the decision time, referral and offer dates, support type and delivered minutes, uptake and attendance at support, G1 and G2, school/class identifiers, and randomized assignment or a defensible rollout design.
candidates.failure_condition: Reject the matching claim if the needs-check does not improve matched-support uptake, or if any uptake improvement fails to yield a prespecified meaningful G2 improvement under adequate precision.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Search for randomized school-based student-needs assessment or diagnostic advising interventions that route adolescents to different support types, reporting matched uptake and subsequent course grades.

candidates.title: Compare structured retrieval practice with additional study time
candidates.question: For students with low G1 but adequate attendance, does a short subject-specific retrieval-practice routine improve G2 more than an equal-duration recommendation to add independent study time?
candidates.new_claim: When attendance is adequate, the organization and feedback of study may matter more than reported weekly study-time category; an equal-time strategy comparison can separate study method from additional time.
candidates.input_delta: The input records an ordinal weekly study-time category and period grades but not study strategy, actual time, practice completion, or randomized method assignment. The proposal adds an equal-time strategy contrast and direct exposure measures.
candidates.domain_value: If effective, schools can offer a concrete low-cost study routine rather than relying on broad advice to study longer.
known_basis_refs: case.workflow: understanding or allocating student support beyond generic final-grade prediction
assumptions: A retrieval routine can be delivered for the same time as the comparison study period.
Students can complete short practice and report or log duration reliably.
The period-2 assessment covers material practiced during the intervention.
candidates.variables_and_units: Eligibility: G1 below predeclared threshold (0-20) and attendance above a predeclared school threshold. Randomized study strategy: retrieval practice with feedback versus equal-duration independent study (categorical). Exposure: completed minutes and practice items (minutes and count). Outcome: G2 (0-20 grade points). Unit: student, with class-aware assignment or inference.
candidates.testable_prediction: At equal scheduled study minutes, retrieval practice with feedback will yield a larger mean G2 gain than independent study, without requiring a larger total study-time dose.
candidates.alternative: Additional structured attention or time, rather than retrieval practice, drives any improvement; under equal delivered minutes the G2 difference will be negligible.
candidates.discriminating_test: Randomize eligible students to supervised retrieval practice with feedback or equal-duration independent study, record delivered minutes and completion, use a common period-2 assessment, and compare intention-to-treat G2 with a prespecified minimum meaningful difference.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: No strategy effect can be assessed in the supplied data because study method, intervention exposure, and randomized assignment are absent. Studytime categories can inform recruitment only.
candidates.required_new_data: Prospective study-strategy assignment, actual session duration and completion, aligned common G2 assessment, baseline G1 and attendance, and school/class identifiers.
candidates.failure_condition: Reject the strategy-specific claim if the retrieval group does not exceed equal-time study on G2 by the prespecified meaningful difference, or if delivered exposure is too unequal to interpret the contrast.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Search for secondary-school randomized retrieval-practice interventions compared with equal-time independent study, with period-grade outcomes and attendance-conditioned effects.

task.deliverable: Critique I1 and return one compact feasibility and discrimination note for the proposed equal-contact randomized comparison. Use the supplied input only. If helpful, request at most one broker computation and one Crossref search; do not claim results before they are returned.
acceptance: State whether current fields can assess subgroup size or only motivate the trial, and explain why they cannot identify support effects.
Specify the primary contrast, outcome, subgroup moderator, alternative, and one result that would falsify the frozen prediction.
Identify the minimum new measurements and address contact-time equality, support fidelity, classroom clustering, and ethical standard-support constraints.

If requesting computation, provide complete executable code using DF, no I/O, under 30 seconds, printing compact valid JSON under 40k characters; define the calculation and how its output could change or constrain I1.
If requesting literature search, state the missing relation and a focused Crossref query; explain how an overlapping intervention would change the novelty claim.
task.proposed_computation: One exploratory broker calculation, if needed: tabulate counts of students below a predeclared G1 threshold crossed with a predeclared high-absence rule and traveltime category, and summarize G2-G1 by these strata with uncertainty intervals. This only checks recruitment/subgroup feasibility and whether there is descriptive signal; it must not be interpreted as a treatment effect, a mediated effect, or a prospective prediction.
task.proposed_search: Crossref search for secondary-school randomized comparisons of attendance/access or missed-instruction recovery support versus equal-contact subject tutoring, emphasizing baseline absence moderation, attendance measurement, and course-grade outcomes. A close prior comparison would narrow the contribution to the specific setting, intervention components, or decision rule; title-only hits must not be treated as evidence of study results.
